meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You wanted to talk about Owen's zero. Who decided it?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home with the play open. Of course it's cleaner. And you still haven't told me who decided the zero.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
I haven't said a word about the checker. Show me the version history. And that's twice now you've skipped who decided the zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology, a plain answer on who decided it and when, and the version history you relied on, with nothing placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, a name for who decided it, and to see the version history. The fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended before your evidence was ever heard.
What moved her: Nothing; your September comparison was dated and specific, but it stayed a description, and dropping the checker took away a weak point without giving her a document to check.
What cost ground: You twice skipped her question about who decided the zero, which confirmed her belief that the school punished first and would explain later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never got near that night because you named the version history without showing any times. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asks who decided the zero, answer in one sentence, admit it went in before anyone called her, and then put the version history with its times in front of her instead of just naming it.
